Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

z3r 0.1.0

First release of z3r, a native R interface to the Z3 theorem prover.

z3r gives R direct access to Z3’s C API: expressions over all of Z3’s theories, incremental solving, optimization, tactics, fixedpoint engines, user propagators and SMT-LIB2. It targets Z3 5.4.1 and builds against every Z3 release from 4.8.13. Functions that need a newer Z3 than the one z3r was built with report the release they need.

Installation

  • configure finds Z3 through PKG_CPPFLAGS and PKG_LIBS, Z3_INCLUDE_DIR and Z3_LIB_DIR, pkg-config or common installation prefixes, and checks that the headers and the library are the same release. On Windows, configure.win accepts an official release archive through Z3_DIR and installs its DLLs and license next to z3r.
  • With Z3R_DOWNLOAD=true, and on R-universe, an installation that finds no usable Z3 downloads the pinned official Z3 5.4.1 release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and installs the library inside the package. Nothing is downloaded otherwise.
  • z3_version() and z3_build_info() report the Z3 release, how it was found, the loaded library and the compiler.

Expressions

  • Sorts: Boolean, integer, real, bit-vector, floating point, rounding mode, string, sequence, regular expression, character, array, set, algebraic datatype, finite domain and uninterpreted sorts, and the complex, finite field and finite set sorts of Z3 5.
  • Exact numerals from strings, R numbers and gmp numbers, with a documented policy for doubles (options(z3r.doubles)). z3_value() converts results to R without loss of precision.
  • R operators and math functions on Z3 terms, with sort checking: arithmetic, comparisons (also lexicographic order on strings), Boolean logic, sqrt(), and a[i] on arrays.
  • Batch construction of constants (z3_ints(), z3_reals(), z3_bools()) and n-ary sums and products (z3_sum(), z3_prod()).
  • Inspection of terms and declarations, substitution, simplification with parameters, quantifiers and lambdas with patterns and weights, and a dictionary keyed by terms (z3_ast_map()).
  • Translation of objects between contexts (z3_translate()) and to and from the symcompR computer algebra package, refusing any conversion that would change the meaning of an expression.

Solving

  • Solvers with assertions, tracked assertions, assumptions, scopes (z3_push(), z3_pop(), z3_with_scope()), unsatisfiable cores, proofs, consequences, cubes, units and trails, congruence classes, solving for variables, initial values, typed parameters and statistics.
  • One-call shortcuts: z3_solve() returns a model or NULL, and z3_prove() returns TRUE or FALSE with a counterexample.
  • z3_check_result() returns the status, model, core, proof, timing, statistics, parameters, a fingerprint of the input and the build in one object, for batches and reports.
  • Models: each z3_model() is an independent copy; values by name (m$x, m[["x"]]), batch evaluation of expressions (z3_eval() with a list) and conversion of all or selected values (z3_model_values()); enumeration of distinct models (z3_all_models()); hand-built models.
  • Per-check timeouts (z3_check(timeout = )) that leave the solver’s other parameters in place, interruption with Ctrl-C, and z3_interrupt() from inside callbacks.
  • Optimization with hard and soft constraints, multiple objectives with priorities, unbounded and non-attained optima, bounds and the best model found when a check returns "unknown", and model callbacks.
  • User propagators, clause callbacks and proof checker callbacks written in R. Errors and interrupts in callbacks are raised in R after the check, and R code never runs on Z3’s worker threads; a result found by a solver copy that could not run the callbacks is refused.

Theories and engines

  • Linear and nonlinear arithmetic, bit-vectors with overflow predicates, IEEE floating point, arrays (multi-index, map, default values, lambdas), sets, strings, sequences, regular expressions and characters.
  • Algebraic datatypes: recursive, mutually recursive, enumerations, tuples, lists and polymorphic datatypes.
  • Uninterpreted and recursive functions, special relations and pseudo-Boolean constraints.
  • Tactics, probes, goals and simplifiers.
  • The fixedpoint engine for constrained Horn clauses (Spacer) and Datalog, with lemma callbacks, external relations, model-based projection and quantifier elimination.
  • Real closed fields, algebraic number arithmetic and polynomial subresultants.
  • SMT-LIB2 parsing, export (with tracked constraints and the inputs of solvers with simplifiers, so the text has the solver’s answer) and the SMT-LIB2 command interpreter; DIMACS export of clausal problems.

Safety

  • Every Z3 object is reference counted and keeps its context alive, so objects can be garbage collected in any order.
  • Z3 errors become R errors. Objects restored from a saved session, and objects from different contexts, are refused with a clear message.
